directory_performance_issue_68.fixture: Disposable reflink/copy of the pinned demo upstream checkout; source files unchanged between runs; warmed state before each measured series.
directory_performance_issue_68.profiles: Both binaries use Cargo release profile with Instant timers around directory fingerprinting and recipe execution. Profiling changes exist only in temporary copies, not committed engine code.
directory_performance_issue_68.method: Run before series, then after series in the same copied checkout. Each begins with an excluded warm-up, then three no-op requests, one forced theme, two forced themes at -j1, and two forced themes at -j2. The measured needfile retained @jobs(2) for the renderer in both series. Directory durations are cumulative timer durations, not exclusive wall time; parallel spans overlap.
limitations: Warm filesystem caches; one machine; before/after series were sequential, not randomized or load-isolated.
Forced builds are single observations. Large recipe-duration variation is not explained by the directory cache; do not attribute the entire forced-build difference to it.
No full 64-theme performance or equivalence rerun; earlier full-output evidence predates this change.
The committed demo now uses @jobs(1), selected from the after-series concurrency comparison; raw -j2 measurements used the prior @jobs(2).
Alternating independent no-op replication showed a smaller gain than the initial series; retain both rather than treating the initial difference as a universal speedup.

independent_noop_replication.method: Same fixture and profiling binaries; alternating B/A/B/A phases, four requests each, first request of each phase excluded as warm-up; six measured requests per binary. Supplied by independent reviewer.

independent_sigterm_probe.scenario: Two roots share one cold atomic directory dependency; SIGTERM during shared recipe.
